newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda plans extra production in May.
newsitem.headline: Mazda plans extra production in May.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp said on Friday it will increase production of its new models by cancelling holidays for the first time since November 1994.

Mazda, which is 33.4 percent owned by Ford Motor Co, will operate three extra days in May by cancelling holidays on May 17, 24 and 31 at its No.2 plant in Hofu, in western Japan's Yamaguchi prefecture, a Mazda spokesman said.
The company is also considering operating several extra days at the No.1 and No.2 plants in Hofu in and after June.
Mazda is due to launch a fully remodelled Capella (called 626 abroad) mid-size car in August, industry sources said.
It hopes to boost domestic sales through the introduction of the Capella, the spokesman said.
Mazda's domestic sales in calendar 1996 fell eight percent from a year earlier to 285,204 units, industry data showed.
